{"title": "[Nimbus Ledger] Recurring lease-renewal oscillation causing periodic write-path stalls in write-coordinator across regions", "summary": "Incident 999000001 tracks a long-running, intermittent lease-renewal oscillation in the Nimbus Ledger write path.
The failure surfaces as bursts of NLX-4207 (lease renewal timeout) followed by NLX-4210 (stale primary) on the write-coordinator, correlated with a sharp rise in p99 write latency lasting 3-30 minutes at a time.

Impact:
  - Customer-visible writes queue for up to 30s per burst.
  - No data loss observed.
  - Automatic self-recovery once one of the candidate primaries wins the lease election cleanly.

Why this incident stayed open so long:
  - Root cause was not isolated until several weeks into the trace. We had working hypotheses (renewal-delay-driven oscillation) but no reproducer.
  - Mitigations reduced blast radius but did not eliminate recurrence.

Regions affected (rolling): westus, eastus, northeu, southasia.

See dashboard: https://dashboards.nimbus-ledger.example.com/incident/999000001
Runbook: https://runbooks.nimbus-ledger.example.net/lease-renewal

Related work items:
  - Work item 9990000021: revert of the 8901 renewal-ack reordering change.
  - Work item 9990000029: separate investigation of the southasia residual pattern.

SCREENSHOTS:"}, {"ChangedBy": "nl-arch-41", "Text": "Karim: writing this up because we've been at it long enough that I want the timeline in one place for anyone coming to this cold.

Rough timeline (all times UTC, all relative to open):
  t+00h   Alex picks up on two short NLX-4207 bursts, both self-cleared before paging arrived. First reading is on the westus lease-manager pool.
  t+02h   Priya's peer-clock-offset hypothesis is posted (claim: 800ms deadline is the trigger).
  t+04h   Priya's 5% canary bumps renewal_timeout to 1200ms on lease-manager in westus. NLX-4207 goes to zero on the canary group only. Canary reverted 40 min in.
  t+05h   I pushed back on the 800ms story. Offset history doesn't support it. Deploy log shows 8901 rolled two weeks ago on write-coordinator to all regions except eastus.
  t+05h   Yuki pulled the per-region NLX-4207 counts and flagged eastus as suspiciously clean.
  t+07h   Ricardo confirmed the build gap: eastus on 8814, everyone else on 8901.
  t+08h   Jamie's counterpoint: eastus is a lower-traffic region, could be load not build.
  t+09h   Jamie loaded eastus to peer-region rate for 90 min. NLX-4207 stayed at 0. So it isn't load.
  t+11h   Handed off to the write-coordinator team for their read on the 8901 diff.
  t+11h..t+18d   Silent period on our side. WCoord team's read: a single change to the renewal-ack path in 8901 reorders the renewal-received callback against the primary-election callback under contention.
  t+18d   Zora (fresh oncall rotation) reverted eastus to 8901 for a controlled confirmation. NLX-4207 pattern on eastus reproduced within 4h. Filed 9990000021 against WCoord.
  t+19d   Fix commit lands as 9901 (targeted revert of the reordering change) and rolls to all regions overnight.
  t+19d   NLX-4207 drops to baseline in westus, eastus, northeu.

What's still open:
  Southasia is NOT clean. It has a low-rate NLX-4207 stream that predates 8901 entirely — I pulled the offset table back past the 8901 rollout and southasia had the same trickle then. So southasia is a separate failure mode wearing the same error code. Its bursts are ~10x smaller, don't correlate with renewal-packet timing, and look correlated with shard placement drift instead.

Metrics reference (all pulled from the nl_lease_events dashboard, 24h window ending at t+19d):
  - westus NLX-4207 rate: baseline 0.2/s, peak 210/s during storms.
  - northeu NLX-4207 rate: baseline 0.3/s, peak 197/s during storms.
  - eastus NLX-4207 rate before revert: 0/s. After revert: peak 84/s within 4h, matching westus and northeu shape.
  - southasia NLX-4207 rate (persistent trickle): baseline 4/s, peak 11/s during unrelated shard rebalances. Never crosses the 40/s threshold that the primary regions crossed.
  - Peer clock offset in the westus lease-manager pool: sustained above 500ms for the whole incident duration. Never below 400ms.

Hypotheses we tested and ruled out along the way:
  - Renewal-timeout hard limit is the trigger (Priya's original read): ruled out by peer-offset history predating this incident with no corresponding NLX-4207 spikes.
  - Load-driven placement drift: ruled out by Jamie's controlled eastus load test at t+09h.
  - Bad routing rule: WCoord team confirmed NL-ROUTING-07 has not changed in 60 days.
  - Corrupt lease-manager state on one region: ruled out by uniform NLX-4207 shape across westus and northeu after the eastus revert.

Runbook steps applied during the trace:
  - Step 4 (drain a lease-manager replica while peers converge): applied twice, no effect on aggregate rate.
  - Step 7 (roll renewal_timeout up temporarily): applied as Priya's diagnostic canary at t+04h only, never as a mitigation.
  - Step 9 (revert last write-coordinator build in affected region): the actual mitigation, applied as 9901 across all four regions overnight at t+18d.

Dashboards touched during investigation:
  - https://dashboards.nimbus-ledger.example.com/incident/999000001
  - https://dashboards.nimbus-ledger.example.com/lease-oscillation-detail
  - https://dashboards.nimbus-ledger.example.net/southasia-placement-drift

Handoff notes for whoever picks up 9990000029 (southasia residual):
  1. Do not treat lease renewal timing as the primary metric there. The signal in southasia is shard placement drift, not renewal.
  2. Look at nl_shard_placement_events grouped by tenant_hash. There is a small population of tenants whose primary shard replicates to a placement that has been marginal for months.
  3. Southasia p99 latency does not correlate with global NLX-4207 rate. Do a separate correlation.
  4. Do not wait on the WCoord team; they own 9901, not 9990000029. Southasia is a placement-service problem, not a build regression.

Recommendation:
  - Mark this incident mitigated on the 9901 rollout.
  - 9901 is a fix for the write-coordinator regression. It explains the westus, northeu, and (post-revert) eastus behavior. It does not explain southasia.
  - Split the southasia residual out to 9990000029 so it gets a proper RCA against the placement service. Its cause is in placement, not in the write-coordinator diff.

Bottom line: what this ticket was opened for — 'recurring lease-renewal oscillation' — is two failures wearing the same error code, and they live in different services. One of them (the primary-region one) is now fixed. The other is still open and belongs on 9990000029, where the placement-service team can diagnose it against their signals.
